findings.cross_file_justification: The new refusal inherits ConfigError. cheval.py's chain walker surfaces this through its fatal ChevalError handler instead of advancing to the next provider.
findings.description: With headless.mode=prefer-cli and agy_opt_in absent or false, a Google invocation now aborts at the first CLI hop even when a valid GOOGLE_API_KEY makes the subsequent HTTP hop usable. The planners still count this voice because their opt-in exclusion applies only to cli-only routing.
findings.failure_mode: The default-off gate turns a usable fallback chain into INVALID_CONFIG, causing an otherwise available Google review voice to fail and the review to become degraded.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove opted-out agy hops during chain planning, preserving available HTTP hops. Also handle AgyOptInRequiredError explicitly in the walker so a gate change after planning can advance safely without making other ConfigError failures walkable.

findings.cross_file_justification: The new raise in complete() is a ConfigError (INVALID_CONFIG, retryable=False). cheval.py's fallback-chain walk (not touched by this diff) treats ConfigError as a hard-abort, not a walkable hop failure, and nothing in the diff teaches the walk to recognise failure_class == 'opt_in_required'.
findings.description: With the gate default-off, every chain that contains the gemini-headless (agy) hop now hard-aborts the whole invocation at that hop instead of walking past it. Under hounfour.headless.mode=prefer-cli the CLI hop is ordered FIRST, so a Google voice with a valid GOOGLE_API_KEY and a reachable gemini-api fallback dies at hop 1 with INVALID_CONFIG. The TS/bash planners (per reviewer context) only treat cli-only routes as 'not planned', so a mixed cli+http Google route is still counted as planned and the result is exactly the DEGRADED outcome FR-1 was meant to remove. The error class docstring says planners read failure_class as 'not planned, never a failed voice', but the only in-process consumer (the chain walk) never inspects it.
findings.failure_mode: Default install (agy_opt_in absent) + prefer-cli + any Google chain with an HTTP fallback → invocation returns INVALID_CONFIG at hop 1; the HTTP fallback is never tried; Bridgebuilder/Flatline count the voice as planned and run DEGRADED.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make the chain walk treat AgyOptInRequiredError (or any ChevalError whose context.failure_class == 'opt_in_required') as a skip-this-hop and continue to the next hop, or have chain resolution drop agy hops when agy_opt_in_enabled() is False so the hop is never planned. Add a cheval-level test: prefer-cli Google chain, gate off, HTTP fallback mocked OK → SUCCESS via gemini-api.

findings.description: resolve_effort() documents and emits FOUR sources (caller, catalog, extra, none), but both the MODELINV emit comment (cheval.py:2834 'caller | catalog | none') and the emit_model_invoke_complete parameter doc (modelinv.py:497-499) enumerate only three. If model-invoke-complete.payload.schema.json (modified in this PR, truncated here) encodes effort_source as that three-value enum, every CLI hop that resolves effort via extra.effort/extra.reasoning_effort emits an envelope that fails trajectory-schema validation.
findings.failure_mode: A claude-headless entry with legacy extra.effort and no params.default_effort produces effort_source='extra'; schema validation of the MODELINV payload (CI or runtime) rejects the record.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'extra' to the schema enum and to both comments, or collapse the extra rung into 'catalog' in the emitted envelope. Add a test asserting the emitted payload validates for each of the four rungs.

findings.description: _effort_on_wire returns the resolved effort for ANY entry that passes _is_cli_entry(), on the assumption that 'a CLI hop passes it through'. Only the claude headless adapter is shown reading request.effort (via _resolve_effort). codex/grok/gemini(agy) headless adapters build fixed argvs with no effort flag, so for those hops effort_effective reports a value that was never on the wire. The same applies to effort_source: the catalog default of the PRIMARY entry is propagated into every fallback hop's CompletionRequest, so a fallback hop reports 'catalog' when its own catalog said nothing.
findings.failure_mode: Telemetry and dry-run output claim an effort was applied on codex/grok/agy hops (and on fallback hops with a different catalog) when it was not; operators tuning cost/latency on that signal are misled.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate the CLI passthrough on the adapter class actually consuming effort (e.g. a class attribute `reads_effort = True` on ClaudeHeadlessAdapter, False on the others) and return None otherwise; or re-resolve effort per hop against the hop's own entry.

findings.description: FR-1 and the docstring say the key is read from `.loa.config.yaml`, but the gate reads `_deep_merge(load_system_defaults(root), load_project_config(root))`. A framework-shipped System-zone default carrying `headless.agy_opt_in: true` would opt every downstream mount in without any operator edit to .loa.config.yaml, defeating the 'deliberate operator choice' guarantee the adapter docstring makes about argv prompt exposure.
findings.failure_mode: A future defaults bump (or a compromised/mistaken System-zone file) flips the gate on for all consumers; the argv-visible prompt exposure returns silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Read only load_project_config(root) for this key (no defaults layer), and add a test that a `headless.agy_opt_in: true` in the System defaults with no project key still reads False.

findings.description: The docstring promises 'a config that cannot be read reads as off: the gate fails closed', but `root = project_root or _find_project_root()` sits OUTSIDE the try/except. If _find_project_root raises (no marker found, permission error walking up), the exception escapes complete()/health_check()/validate_config() as a raw non-ChevalError instead of a refusal. Separately, the gate re-walks the cwd and re-parses YAML on every complete() and health_check() call. Also note PyYAML (YAML 1.1) treats `agy_opt_in: yes`/`on` as boolean True while the yq-v4 bash/TS readers treat them as strings, so the Python gate opens for a value the planners consider off.
findings.failure_mode: A dispatch from a cwd with no project root crashes with an unhandled exception rather than AgyOptInRequiredError; `agy_opt_in: yes` yields a Python adapter that dispatches while planners never plan it.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the root lookup inside the try. Document/normalise the accepted literal to `true` only (reject YAML-1.1 truthy words by checking the raw scalar, or make the TS/bash readers accept the same set). Consider caching per (root, mtime).

findings.description: For a measured entry the test sets `cap = entry['effective_input_ceiling']` and then asserts `effective == min(cap, cw - dmt)`, which reduces to `effective <= cw - dmt` — already asserted on the next line. The 'computed, not a constant' property is no longer checked for calibrated entries. Likewise test_write_operator_set_changes_only_the_entry_and_replaces_the_shortcut (test_ceiling_probe_cli_transport.py) skips whenever the live catalog is calibrated, which the head catalog now is (936K per test_no_literal_opus55_ceiling_pins.py), so the only test that validates the writer against the REAL catalog shape and the v3 schema never runs. Also test_legacy_wall... now asserts _lookup_max_input_tokens == the catalog's own value, which is circular.
findings.failure_mode: A regression in the writer or in how the real catalog's calibrated entry is laid out passes CI silently; the I2-relative check for measured entries is the only remaining guard.
findings.suggested_fix: For measured entries assert `effective == min(cal.measured_input_tokens, cw - dmt)` (the clamp rule the writer implements) instead of using the entry's own value as the cap. Run the writer test against a pre-probe fixture copy of the real catalog (strip the calibration block in the test) rather than skipping.

findings.description: (Catalog file truncated from this view; based on the tests and reviewer context.) claude-opus-5-5's anthropic HTTP entry is now a CALIBRATED 936K bound (source operator_set, method probed_headless) derived from a Bedrock claude-headless measurement whose probe outcome was `partial`, while the probe tool's own contract (test docstring: 'Only a clean outcome writes the catalog') forbids writing partial results. The calibrated basis is never lowered by observations, and provenance records sample_size: null despite samples existing. The API transport (direct api.anthropic.com, org ITPM limits) was not what was measured.
findings.failure_mode: routing/ceiling.input_bound returns 936K for the HTTP hop; a ~500K-token review goes to the API, hits a 429 ITPM or 400 at the account tier, and the chain walks/fails on every large input with no self-correction, where the previous 180K cap would have refused/chunked up front.
findings.suggested_fix: Either revert the entry to conservative_default until an API-transport (--transport api) clean probe lands, or record source/method honestly (transport: claude-headless, host_route: bedrock, outcome: partial, sample_size: 5) and have input_bound treat a non-API-transport calibration as advisory (min with the policy cap) for the HTTP adapter.
